{{short description|Mathematician}}
'''Christine Elizabeth Heitsch''' is a mathematician whose research involves the [[biomolecular structure]] of [[RNA]].{{r|sinews|alum}} She is a professor of mathematics in the [[Georgia Tech]] School of Mathematics, and the founding director of the Southeast Center for Mathematics and Biology at Georgia Tech.{{r|center}}

==Education and career==
Heitsch graduated in 1994 from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]], ''[[Latin honors|magna cum laude]]'' and [[Phi Beta Kappa]], with a bachelor's degree in mathematics.{{r|alum|cv}}
She completed her Ph.D. at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 2000. Her dissertation, ''Computational Complexity of Generalized Pattern Matching'', was jointly supervised by [[John Rhodes (mathematician)|John Rhodes]] and [[John R. Stallings]].{{r|cv|mg}}

After postdoctoral research at the [[University of British Columbia]] and the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]], she joined the Georgia Tech faculty in 2006, and was promoted to full professor in 2016. At Georgia Tech, as well as being a professor of mathematics, she also holds courtesy appointments in the School of Computational Science & Engineering, and in the School of Biology.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
In 2019 the University of Illinois Department of Mathematics gave Heitsch their annual Alumni Award for Outstanding Professional Achievement.{{r|alum}}
